title: Census of India 1961, District Census Handbook Bikaner (1966): tehsil map 'Teh. Lunkaransar' (PDF page 266)
what_it_contains: Village-boundary map of Lunkaransar tehsil, every village polygon numbered with its 1961 location code (boxed = unpopulated). Codes 1-79 equal the 1971 codes; from 80 on, 1961 = 1971+1 (1961: 80 Khokhrana, 81 Birmana, 82 Motolai, 83 Lakhawar, 84 Ajeetmana, 85 Karnali). The printed graticule ticks (73 30', 73 45', 74 00', 28 45', 28 30') are not reliable (median error 7.6 km); georeferenced instead with 54 village control points (affine, median residual 2.0 km).
why_relevant: Only map found that shows the actual LAND of each pre-range village. Overlaying OSM way 412765540 on it: the range polygon follows village boundaries and contains 27 village polygons at >=85% plus the small parcels 19, 20, 22, 32, 40, i.e. exactly the 32 villages that vanish from the census by 1991, plus about 42% of Birmana (81). Gives land locations for villages never printed on the AMS map (Cheedasar, Beranwala, Likhmisar, Kankraliya, the three Rekh parcels).

title: Census of India 1971, District Census Handbook Bikaner Part X-A/B (1972): Map No. 2.3 'Lunkaransar Tehsil' (PDF page 177) and tehsil amenities map (page 178)
what_it_contains: Tehsil map 'based upon Survey of India map' (1966 copyright) with village names, 1971 location codes, population-size dots (not abadi sites, per map note) and dashed village boundaries. Pages rotated 90 deg; saved rotated upright. Georeferenced with 55 control points (AMS/GNS/OSM); local 7-point affine, leave-one-out median error 2.4 km.
why_relevant: Second independent census map giving positions for every revenue village of 1971, including those unlabeled on the 1955 AMS sheets. No village named Nathor, Machhranwali, Tidasar, Kachrana or Chakdo appears anywhere on it.

title: Census 1971 DCH Bikaner: Lunkaransar tehsil amenities map (PDF page 178)
what_it_contains: Companion map to Map 2.3 showing amenities by village (schools, wells, roads).
why_relevant: Same base map; saved for completeness, not yet read in detail.

title: Census of India 2011, Rajasthan Series 09 Part XII-A, DCH Bikaner (DH_2011_0803_PART_A_DCHB_BIKANER.pdf): Tehsil Lunkaransar map (PDF page 112, printed p.105)
what_it_contains: 13.4 MB PDF, 578 pages (kept in scratchpad, not repo; sha256 4cea5c3ec45ef2c77c098947bd50aad05eccd4f4c4042948fcb59da4af0ec169). Page 112 shows the range as one blank uninhabited village polygon 069202 inside Lunkaransar tehsil; pages 118-140 list villages with 2001 and 2011 codes (row 90: Mahajan Fieldfiring Range 069202 / 00509900).
why_relevant: Official 2011 depiction of the range as a census 'village'. Georeferenced with 23 surviving villages (affine RMS 1.9 km). Area of the blank polygon measured on the map: about 135,750 ha; OSM way 412765540 area 135,996 ha; census figure 136,406 ha. East and south edges agree with OSM; the west edge differs by several km, most likely distortion of the schematic tehsil map (surviving villages such as Kharbara fall inside the drawn blank area).
found_via: census NADA API search 'Bikaner Part XII A'

title: Census 1981 DCH Bikaner Part XIII-A&B: 'Tehsil: Lunkaransar' map page (PDF page 153)
what_it_contains: The page carries only the caption 'TEHSIL : LUNKARANSAR'; the map itself (probably a fold-out) was not scanned; page 154 blank.
why_relevant: The 1981 tehsil village map, closest in date to acquisition, is missing from the online scan; a printed copy (census library) would show it.

title: AMS Series U502 India and Pakistan 1:250,000, Sheet NH 43-9 'Mailsi' (1st ed. AMS, printed 7-59)
what_it_contains: Sheet covering 29-30N, 72-73.5E, downloaded directly (5000x3930 px). Neatline corners in pixels: TL(287,278)=72E/30N, TR(4183,284)=73.5E/30N, BL(266,3258)=72E/29N, BR(4201,3261)=73.5E/29N; bilinear georef; checked against 5 NGA GNS points (0.2-0.5 km). Settlements read near the range: Surjansar, Gomewali, Kupli, Bhagsar, Khal, Narawali, Dhaba, Lunia, Karanpura, Bharuki Dhani.
why_relevant: Completes the 4-sheet AMS set. The OSM range polygon does not enter this sheet at all (polygon max latitude at 73.5E is 28.993N), so NH 43-9 cannot hold any range village; the unlabeled villages must be sought on NH 43-13/14 (where they are not printed) or on the census maps.

title: GeoNames India dump (IN.zip), filtered to 28.3-29.4N, 72.8-74.2E
villages_named: hindor (only a namesake at 29.096N 73.866E, Suratgarh side, OUTSIDE)
what_it_contains: 346 features in the box (201 PPL). Only 7 settlements lie inside the range polygon: Thotya, Rāmpura, Motāsur, Kuināna, Hāthusar, Dewāsar, Lakhor Chhoti. None of the unresolved names occur. IN.zip 15.7 MB sha256 e59b47a3...527bda (scratchpad).
why_relevant: Confirms positions of 7 range villages; shows GeoNames inherits the sparse NGA/AMS set; flags namesakes (Hindor, Likhmisar, Kumbhasar elsewhere) that can mislead.

title: NGA GEOnet Names Server (GNS), public ArcGIS REST layer, India (cc_ft='IND') records in 28.3-29.4N, 72.8-74.2E
what_it_contains: 370 name records (320 N, 46 V variants). The old per-country zip (earth-info.nga.mil/gns/html/cntyfile/in.zip) is gone (404); the REST query works without login (where=cc_ft='IND' AND lat/long box; the envelope query timed out). Name-pattern searches across India for Nathor, Machh*, Tida*, Kachran*, Chakd*, Kolan*, Chudan*, Dhanna*, Likhmi*, Kumbhasar etc. found no match in or near the range; no 'historical' or terminated entries here.
why_relevant: Rules out GNS as a source for the unresolved names; its entries here match the AMS sheets within 0.2-0.5 km (GNS was compiled from them).

title: Wikidata SPARQL box query (73.1-74.0E, 28.4-29.2N)
what_it_contains: 107 items, almost all railway stations, bank branches and fuel pumps; no village item for any range village. One item (HDFC Bank Lunkaransar branch Q132165114) is wrongly geocoded inside the range at 28.628N 73.614E.
why_relevant: Shows Wikidata has no items for the 34 villages: a gap the project could fill.

title: OpenStreetMap places via Overpass (kumi.systems mirror) and Nominatim, 28.45-29.15N, 73.2-73.95E
villages_named: nathor? (Nathuwas hamlet n7335802789 at 28.5073N 73.2631E, OUTSIDE, 9.9 km)
what_it_contains: 204 elements: inside the polygon only 7 locality nodes (AMS-style spellings) plus military landuse ways. Outside: Ajeetmana, Karnali, Khokharana, Birmana (0.1 km outside), Rekh Megana, Chak Jor, Nathuwas hamlet etc. Nominatim found none of the unresolved names in Rajasthan.
why_relevant: Current map layer; the 'Nathuwas' hamlet SW of the range is the only hit for any alias of Nathor (could be a resettlement dhani or unrelated).

title: OSM way 412765540 'Mahajan Field Firing Ranges' compared with census areas
what_it_contains: Polygon area computed here: 135,996 ha (equirectangular at 28.8N). Census 1991: 136,411 ha; 2011: 136,406 ha; sum of the 32 villages in 1981: 135,171 ha.
why_relevant: Polygon area matches the census range area within 0.3%, and on the 1961 village map its edge follows old village boundaries: it is a good proxy for the acquired land.

title: Soviet General Staff topographic maps 1:100k/1:200k (vlasenko mirror); target sheets H-43-100, 111, 112, 123, 124 (1:100k) and H-43-XXVI, XXXII (1:200k)
what_it_contains: Host returns 503 upstream timeout (HTTP) and connection reset (HTTPS); download.maps.vlasenko.net does not resolve. loadmap.net returns 'Forbidden'; mapstor.com is a paid shop; satmaps.info covers ex-USSR; poehali.org unreachable; web.archive.org blocked from this machine.
why_relevant: Soviet 1:100k sheets would show many more hamlets (dhanis) than AMS 1:250k and could hold Nathor/Machhranwali/Tidasar/Kachrana/Chakdo. A human should open the sheet list in a normal browser.
found_via: sheet IDs computed from H-43 grid

title: Wikimapia, range area
what_it_contains: API returns 'Invalid key'; the site sets a cookie by JavaScript before serving (bot check). Not bypassed.
why_relevant: Users often tag abandoned villages on Wikimapia; a human should browse the area and note any tagged 'old village' places.

title: Survey of India Open Series Maps (onlinemaps / Nakshe)
what_it_contains: Free OSM sheets need registration and login (Nakshe host did not respond). Relevant 1:50k sheets are in degree sheet 44H (28-29N, 73-74E) and 44G for the strip north of 29N.
why_relevant: Modern SoI sheets may show the range boundary and relict names; needs a human with an account.

title: USGS EarthExplorer declassified CORONA/KH imagery
what_it_contains: Search and metadata export require a USGS login; not attempted. Corona Atlas (corona.cast.uark.edu) covers the Middle East only.
why_relevant: 1960s-70s CORONA frames would show every abadi before 1982; a human with a free USGS account should search 28.55-29.04N, 73.30-73.80E and record entity IDs.

title: ISRO Bhuvan public layers
what_it_contains: Main site redirects; WMS hosts (bhuvan-vec1/vec2) did not answer; data download needs login.
why_relevant: Village boundary layers could show whether any old revenue boundaries survive in state GIS.

title: Wayback Machine
what_it_contains: Connection reset for every request from this machine (web.archive.org and wayback.archive.org); archive.org itself works.
why_relevant: Wayback copies of vlasenko and Wikimapia could not be tried.

title: Census 1971 Administrative Atlas, Part IX-A, Rajasthan (1976); also Census Atlas 1961 (28142), 1981 (28457), Admin Atlas 2011 (45)
what_it_contains: Found in NADA search, not downloaded (likely large, tehsil-level only).
why_relevant: May show the Lunkaransar tehsil boundary change and, in 1981/2011, the range; lower priority than the DCH tehsil maps.

title: Gazetteer of the Bikanir State (Powlett, 1874), archive.org copy wbsl.16155 (also dli.csl.8190)
what_it_contains: Alternative archive.org identifiers for the 1874 gazetteer whose DLI copy failed earlier; may include a state map.
why_relevant: Second route to the Powlett gazetteer and any map in it.
